restrictions: The two messages have 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 bytes for one t with 1 <= t < 2^32: t zero chunks of 1024 bytes followed by a last chunk of one block. The last chunk is compressed as a non-root chunk with counter t (v12 = t, v13 = 0), flags 3 and its true block length; the 63-byte block ends in eight zero bytes, so words 14 and 15 and the top byte of word 13 are zero in both zero-filled blocks. Equal last-chunk chaining values give equal digests by the tree lemma of proof.md Section 7.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision between two distinct complete messages.

Exact part: for every trial of proof.md Section 8 the two last-chunk chaining values agree on words 0, 2, 5 and 7, E1.c1 lies in the cube of beta* = 18b0e098 so that beta = beta* in every trial, Y4 ranges over the whole class of eta (524,288 values; no sub-class, no rule on h1), and the counter t is solved per trial as ROL(K0.d1,16) XOR K0.a1; trials with t = 0 are skipped. The search continues only in outer steps that pass the exact filter of proof.md Section 8 for the six listed E1 outcomes S = {175,185,275,285,385,685}020a0 (share 279,070,422,111 / 2^48 = 2^-9.9782); of these, the joint solver sees only those kept by the exact s-pattern pre-check, and its guards (G7) and (G15) drop only words that hold no success, so by Lemmas F, VP, G7 and G15 none of these steps loses a counted success. The eight other outcomes of beta* are not counted as successes.

Heuristic part: under H1', H4', H5_exec and H_G_cluster, each stated for the advice record of proof.md Section 12, with probability at least 0.39 the search finds a trial whose remaining 128 chaining-value bits also agree. It walks 2^90.117 trials: 2^50.117 contexts (proof.md 9.8), each the seven outer words of one fresh draw, times the 2^19 members of the class, times the 2^21 trials of an outer step.

Machine: a classical word RAM with 256-bit words under collision-frontier-v5, 430 machine units (operations, loads, stores) to the unit, 64 registers and constants as immediates; fetching a word from memory is a load. Charges (proof.md 9.8, 11; GPT Sol answers CD and CM 5A): 600 units per context, which draws its fresh word and runs the 39 member-free lines of step CO once; 66 units per batch of seven members in packed 36-bit lanes (42 for the last batch of three partners of a cluster), which computes the 8 member lines on which omega depends and tests every lane against the direct table T2; 57 units once per batch with a lane whose test-(2) mask meets S (the fill: its count in a register and halt, and the 17 lines on which only Y9 depends, in 16 packed lines, for all lanes, kept as the batch's cached Y9); and 10 units for each such lane (its E count in a register and the test of its cached Y9 against T1).

Cluster gate (proof.md 9.9, Lemmas KP, A9, CL and OR; GPT Sol answers CI 1, CJ 1 to 5 and CK 5): the 32 members that differ only in bits 10 to 14 of e1 form a cluster, and all have omega mod 2^9 in two values computed from the representative; a fixed table P of 2^21 words (built once for 2^27 units) skips the cluster, with no read of T2, when neither value can pass test (2), losing nothing. Charges: 74 units per batch of seven representatives (pair 3, omega side 19, gate key 8, seven gate tests 41, cursor 3; 56 for the last of a context; 2,341 per context) and 333 per opened cluster (partner batches 4 * 66 + 42, nesting 21 with the eight words and opened count in registers, T2 test 6). The run halts when the opened count passes A_BUDGET = 9,189,056,937,678,035,781, and the time bound charges A_BUDGET + 1. No premise: Lemma OR proves that for uniform outer words the gate opens on at most 0.45936866663 of the clusters on average, so the budget is passed with probability at most exp(-20).

Building T1 and T2, one entry per 32-bit word, costs below 2^39 units once (2^38 bytes). A passing lane is charged 508 units, its rebuild, the 30 words and 10 reserved registers saved around the solver (the cached Y9 among them), pre-check, the three words of (G7) and its preflight included. When the pre-check keeps outcomes T, the solver with the guards (G7) and (G15), its global ledger of 1,024 and the root certificates (120 units a root) starts only if the credit left covers its metered cap CM(T) <= 17,714, and a meter in the 64th register debits each executed block's unit cost plus one; the debit lies between the executed ledger U and CM(T) and is at most 10191/10016 U (Lemma ME). The credit is 861,108,186,818,977,910,726 units. These are proved upper allowances of a specified layout, not measured counts. Nothing is sorted, every word-indexed read is charged as a load, and the tables do not grow with the trials.

Halts: the run stops with failure as soon as the opened-cluster count, the test-(2) count, the fill count or the pass count passes its budget, as soon as a metered cap CM(T) is larger than the credit left, and after RUN_CONTEXTS = 1,220,926,580,812,448 contexts. The time bound charges each budget plus one, RUN_CONTEXTS + 1 contexts, all 2,341 * RUN_CONTEXTS representative batches and the whole credit, so it holds for every run (proof.md Sections 9, 11).

This package is our entry 415e792c with the member loop and the direct tables of entry e9b6649e (hecmas), the guard (G7) of our entry 0bc5f130, the omega-first batch (GPT Sol, answer CA, audited in answer CD), the E count in a register, the root certificate, the guard (G15), the global ledger of 1,024 (answers CD and CF), the cluster gate in its tight layout (CI 1, CJ 1 to 5), budgets at our sample's least factors with proved reserves over contexts (CK), the metered credit (CK3) and the cached Y9 per batch (CM). Randomness: one fresh uniform 256-bit word per context. Since each context visits each member of the class once or skips it in a cluster that fails test (2) (Lemmas CX and CL), means over outer steps equal those of a uniform outer step; independence holds between contexts only. H1' (ii) and H_G_cluster are therefore stated per context. Success 0.39 holds only under H1', H4', H5_exec and H_G_cluster.

The factor 125,920,632,087 in H1' is ten elevenths of the model's conditional count of the six listed outcomes on the class, rounded down, and is not measured by the organizer-run experiment, which executes the search on one context per trial and returns root-instance pairs (counter 0, flags 11): no digest experiment can show a half-collision of a non-root chunk's chaining value. The cluster gate, the filter, the pre-check, (G7) and (G15) lose nothing; the two count shares matter only for the budgets (H4'), the mean fills only for the fill budget (H_G_cluster) and the mean executed ledger only for the credit (H5_exec). No full 2-round collision is exhibited.

The declared program experiments/frontline.py executes the search of proof.md 9.1 on one context per organizer trial, 32 clusters each: the walk by clusters with the gate, the direct-table tests (entries computed on demand by the rules that fill the tables), the E lanes with the fill and cached Y9 of each batch, the pre-check, the preflight and the meter, the joint solver with (G7) and (G15), the root certificate, and the budgets, credit and halts of this row, with the units of proof.md Section 11 added per event; in the same run it checks every walked member against a straight-line recomputation, every cached Y9 against a fresh one and every metered debit against the ledger (proof.md 9.2). Its observations are its own counts. No root of the search occurs at that scale. The participant programs cited in proof.md 9.8 and Section 13 are not part of the package.

Fixed nonuniform advice, stated in full in proof.md Section 12: the six 32-bit constants of 3.2, eta = 830303cf, beta* = 18b0e098 with the mask 0e09818b and value 02008000 of its cube, the seven tau values and eps = 6e21be55 of the filter's automata and the mask 5f of S, 73 bytes (nonuniform_advice_log2_bytes 7). The success analysis uses only properties of this stated record that proof.md verifies exactly: Fact P (3.2), Lemma Q, Theorem C (iii) and (iv), the table of 10.1 with the program of Section 17, the certificate of the filter for S (Section 8), and the pre-check patterns and solver guards, trees and caps for this class (9.4, 9.7, 11). H1', H4', H5_exec and H_G_cluster are stated for this record and none concerns how it was found; no premise concerns what any selection returns. The selection procedure SEL that found it is charged in full as preprocessing (preprocessing_log2).

preprocessing_log2 55, included in time_log2, is the charge of the selection procedure SEL of proof.md Section 12, which found the advice: 116 solver runs capped at 2^56 operations each, one count per model capped at 2^52 (+ 2^10), and the choice of S capped at 2^50, in all S_old = 8,882,224,365,081,579,520 operations, below 2^62.946, below 2^54.198 units, rounded up to 55. The cap holds by construction, since every run halts at its cap; that SEL returns exactly the stored values rests on the participant's solver log and recounts, which are not in the package. The cost model charges any search omitted from the submitted program; SEL is that search, and its whole capped cost is charged. The search alone is below 2^63.5161 units. memory_log2_bytes 44 covers, all held at once (sum below 2^44), the two output messages (each below 2^42 bytes), the search with its code and direct tables (below 2^39 bytes) and every run of SEL (below 2^34 + 2^20 bytes). No priority or novelty claim is made.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical. Stated for the instance that the advice record of proof.md Section 12 fixes, and for no other. The run has RUN_CONTEXTS independent contexts, each the seven outer words of one fresh uniform 256-bit word, and every context visits all 2^19 members of the class, except the members of clusters that the gate of proof.md 9.9 skips, which fail test (2) and hold no listed good trial (Lemmas CX and CL). Let N_o be the number of listed good valid trials of one outer step (t != 0, R = 0, and an E1 outcome in S = {175,185,275,285,385,685}020a0, six outcomes of beta*; Y4 in the whole class of eta; no rule on h1), counted over all of Q* whether or not the outer step passes the filter or the pre-check, and N_c its sum over the 2^19 outer steps of a context. (i) For a uniform outer step U (seven uniform outer words, a uniform member), E[N_o(U)] >= (2^21 - 1) q with q = FACTOR * 2^-128, FACTOR = floor(10 * 138,512,695,296 / 11) = 125,920,632,087, about 2^-91.126 (just under ten elevenths of the conditional model rate p of Lemma S1 for S); by Lemma CX (c), E[N_c] = 2^19 E[N_o(U)], so (i) is the statement of entry 415e792c. (ii) With the context as the unit, as entry e9b6649e declares it: the probability that no valid trial of the run is a listed good trial is at most exp(-0.49676) + 0.001; that is, listed good trials are not clustered, neither among the trials of one outer step nor among the outer steps (members) of one context, beyond what this bound allows. Given (i), rho_c = E[N_c(N_c-1)]/E[N_c] <= 0.0065 is sufficient for (ii) by Lemma S8 applied to the independent contexts. rho_c = rho_w + rho_x, where rho_w is the per-step factorial ratio of entry 415e792c and rho_x >= 0 the part that pairs of different members of one context add, so this clause is stronger than the per-step clause of entry 415e792c. Part (ii) is an assumption: rho_c is not measured and cannot be measured at full size (proof.md 10.3). This restates the rate-and-dependence premise of entry 26ebba63 for the whole class, S and the walk by contexts; that entry's clause was for the sub-class of 2^17 members with rule A and seven outcomes and does not by itself imply this law (GPT Sol, answer AT 2). It is declared here anew. By Lemma F every listed good trial lies in an outer step that passes the filter, by Lemma CL the cluster gate skips none, by Lemma VP the pre-check skips none and by Lemmas G7 and G15 the guards (G7) and (G15) drop none, so N_o is the same count, pointwise (GPT Sol, answer AW 1).
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Sections 8 and 9: lengths 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 with a non-root last chunk (counter t, v13 = 0, flags 3), the six constants of Section 3.2, Y4 ranging over all 524,288 members of the class of eta (Lemma Q) inside every context, a context being the seven outer words of one fresh 256-bit word of the run (proof.md 9.8, Lemma CX); in every trial E1.c1 is drawn from the cube of beta* = 18b0e098, and t is solved per trial, with t = 0 skipped. The search continues only in outer steps that pass the exact filter of Section 8 for S, the solver sees only those that the pre-check of 9.7 keeps, and it applies the guards (G7) and (G15); N_o counts all of Q* in every outer step and only the six outcomes of S.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the participant's exact count, in integer arithmetic under the seven-word model of Section 10 with Y4 uniform in the class, of the part of beta* on the class carried by the six outcomes of S (67,633,152 = 1,032 * 2^16 on the per-trial scale 2^-83 of the class; the counting program and the six rows of its output are printed in Section 17), times 2^11 for drawing E1.c1 from the cube (Lemma S1), taken at ten elevenths, rounded down. The filter, the pre-check, (G7) and (G15) change neither the count nor the premise (Lemmas S9 (b), VP, G7 and G15). Participant evidence of Section 13, untrusted by the harness: a whole-class graphics-card run of 2^46 real counter trials in 2^25 passing outer steps, with a sub-class control of the same size, in which every measured quantity matches the exact model within 1.5 clustered standard errors, among them the E1 rate on the whole class of the seven outcomes of entry 59f8915e, 1.0020 +- 0.0086 of the model (13,595 events), and its ratio to the sub-class rate, 0.9895 +- 0.0120 (model 1); the E1 event of S is a sub-event of that measured event (52/53 of it in the model); and a reduced-width (8-bit) end-to-end run of complete messages, with no sub-class and no rule, in which the counter arrangement found 251 collisions against 255.0 predicted, and, in a preregistered rerun, 40,882 against 40,800.63 (1.00199 +- 0.00496; one-sided 97.7 per cent lower bound 0.99213, above 10/11, the rule fixed in advance for this factor). At 32 bits the joint 128-bit event itself, about 2^-91 per trial, is not measured. Dependence (proof.md 10.3 and Section 13, participant runs on the counter instance made after the design): part (ii) is assumed, not measured. Under the model E[N_c] is about 2^-51.126, and rho_x is about v * E[N_c], where v is the clustering ratio of listed good trials by context (1 for independent members); so (ii) fails only if v exceeds about 2^44, or if one listed good trial makes another in the same context far more likely than its rate. Evidence that v is near 1: the same ratio, (E[n(n-1)]/E[n]) / ((2^19 - 1) p_hat) for per-context counts of events that every listed good trial meets, is 1.1513 for the filter pass, 1.1572 for the pass with the pre-check and 1.153 for an outer step whose solver reaches a leaf (120,000 contexts; control arms of independent outer steps 1.0000, 1.0000 and 0.998), and 1.2486 +- 0.0806 for an outer step whose solver returns a root (46,104,576 contexts; control 1.0367 +- 0.0718); it does not grow with depth beyond the errors. The clustering comes from condition (2), whose omega has w8 fixed by the context. Preregistered (proof.md Section 13; 262,144 contexts and 2^46 trials per arm, two generators, a control arm): the cross-member factor Rx is 0.999 +- 0.054 (upper limit 1.162) for the listed E1 outcome, 2^-32.29 per trial, 0.90 +- 0.24 (upper limit 1.94) for (J1) and (J2) of the E3 half, 2^-34.58, and 1.0002 for R24, 2^-23.76; only the filter events cluster (1.144, 1.152); every upper limit lies at least 43 bits below the 2^43.86 that the clause allows.
heuristics.limitations: The factor 125,920,632,087 is assumed (ten elevenths of the model count of the six outcomes of S on the class, rounded down). The premise of entry 26ebba63 was for the sub-class with rule A; it is not inherited, and the whole-class law of N_o for S is declared, not proved. The organizer-run experiment executes the search on one context per trial and returns root-instance pairs (counter 0, flags 11); it measures neither the factor nor the counter half-collision, which no digest experiment can show. Part of the transfer of the single-trial law to the actual sampler is proved (Lemmas S1-S5, S8, S9, VP, G7 and G15) and part is assumed in (i). Part (ii) is an assumption: the bound rho_c <= 0.0065 is not measured and cannot be measured at full size, since a context holds a listed good trial with probability about 2^-51.126; the proved cap of 16 listed good trials in one outer step (Lemmas CV, G7 and G15) does not help at this run length. Stated for contexts, it is stronger than a per-step clause, since it adds the cross-member part rho_x. The clustering ratios that support it are measured for events that every listed good trial meets, from the filter to the roots of the solver (one generator, after the design) and, preregistered with two generators, the two halves of a listed good trial, not for listed good trials: the joint event, about 2^-91 per trial, is not reachable, so carrying Rx near 1 to it remains the premise. The whole-class graphics-card run measures the E1 side of the seven outcomes together and the filter, not the six of S on their own, not the E3 side nor the joint event. Lemmas F, VP, G7, G15 and S9 (a) use no law of the words; the 8-bit end-to-end run has no filter. The 8-bit runs are evidence under the model's uniform free words, not at 32 bits.

heuristics.statement: Supporting; stated for the advice record of proof.md Section 12. For an outer step of the run let I_E be 1 when its test-(2) mask meets S and I_2 be 1 when it passes the filter for S. Premise: for a uniform outer step U, and hence for the mean over the outer steps of one context (Lemma CX (c)), Pr(I_E(U) = 1) <= 1.000026 * 233,715,456 / 2^32 and Pr(I_2(U) = 1) <= 1.000176 * 279,070,422,111 / 2^48, the exact shares of Section 8 (2^-4.1998 and 2^-9.9782) times the declared factors. Use, proved given the premise: each budget is its premise mean over the RUN_STEPS = 640,117,155,200,996,737,024 outer steps, rounded up, plus 2^19 s with s = ceil(sqrt(10 RUN_CONTEXTS)): E_BUDGET = 34,833,655,546,458,722,911 E lanes and PASS_BUDGET = 634,818,459,892,147,173 passing outer steps. Both counts add up independent per-context counts between 0 and 2^19 (Lemma CX), so Hoeffding's inequality over the contexts bounds each overflow by exp(-2 s^2 / RUN_CONTEXTS) <= exp(-20); with the credit, fill and opened-cluster tails, all five lie within the allowance 0.0005. Reaching a budget halts with failure; the time bound charges each budget plus one. The number of outer steps that reach the solver has no budget: the solver is paid from the credit of H5exec-executed-solver-work (GPT Sol, answer AW 5).
heuristics.scope: The counts N_E and N_2 of proof.md 10.3, taken over all RUN_STEPS outer steps, every member of every context (9.1, 9.8): per context, each count lies between 0 and 2^19, the contexts are independent, and the mean per context is 2^19 times the indicator's probability for a uniform outer step (Lemma CX (c)); the two indicators of one outer step may depend on each other in any way.
heuristics.extrapolation: The nominal shares are exact for uniform independent (Y9, omega) (GPT Sol, answers AC, AN and AW 3; the certificate of Section 8). The factors are the least on a grid of one part per million that pass a lower-tail Chernoff test at exp(-7), (m - k)^2 >= 14 m with m = 2^39 * factor * share, on the counts of our preregistered sample of 2^39 real outer steps of the whole class (proof.md 10.3 and Section 13): 29,915,698,553 test-(2) lanes against 29,915,578,368 and 545,067,537 passing steps against 545,059,418.18 (GPT Sol, answer CK 2.1); in exact rational arithmetic each factor passes and the one a part per million lower fails. Other measurements (Section 13, untrusted by the harness, whole class): on 60,000,000 real outer steps the two counts are 1.0004 +- 0.0005 (test (2)) and 0.9980 +- 0.0041 (pass) of their nominal values; with the member loop, 120,000 contexts with all 2^19 members each: pass share 0.99847 and test-(2) share 0.99868 of nominal. The declared experiment reports its E lanes and passes per trial (proof.md 9.2: 0.0546 of cluster members over 4,096 trials in the participant's run).
heuristics.limitations: The bounds on the indicators' probabilities are not proved: Y9 and omega are not proved independent and uniform. The factors rest on one preregistered sample from one pseudorandom generator (Philox4x32-10) under an independent-draw reading of the Chernoff test, which is an evidence limitation, not a proof of the physical means. The time bound, the filter and the pre-check do not depend on these shares; if a budget is reached the run halts with failure, which lowers the success probability only.

heuristics.statement: Supporting; stated for the advice record of proof.md Section 12. This is the premise H5_exec of GPT Sol's answer CK3. For an outer step of the run, before any halt, let U be the ledger of its call of steps 2 and 3 (proof.md 9.7): A(T) = 1,024 + 2,304 F + 1,408 r for the outcomes T = X AND VMASK[nu] that its pre-check keeps (r rows, F families), plus the unit cost of every block that the joint solver with (G7) and (G15) and the root certificate execute on its words (20 per forced node, 48 per free node, 4 per selected node, 64 per node at position 15, 80 per leaf, 120 per root); U = 0 when T is empty or the step does not pass the filter. Premise: for a uniform outer step, and hence for the mean over the outer steps of one context (Lemma CX (c)), E[U] <= 1.01 * u_M, where u_M = 92,113,900,425,963 / 2^46 = 1.3090172562... It concerns the joint law of all the words the solver reads, not T alone. Use, proved given the premise (GPT Sol, answer CK3 3 and 4): by Lemma ME the meter debits V with U <= V <= CM(T) <= 17,714 and V <= 10191/10016 U in every call, whatever the words, so no second premise is needed. The credit starts at CREDIT = m_C + ceil(sqrt(40 L_C m_C)) + 14 L_C + 17,714 = 861,108,186,818,977,910,726, with m_C = ceil(10191/10016 * 1.01 * RUN_STEPS * u_M) = 861,090,301,331,536,512,780, L_C = 17,714 * 2^19 the most one context can debit and 17,714 the preflight reserve. The per-context sums of debits are independent, lie between 0 and L_C and have total mean at most m_C, so Bernstein's inequality over contexts puts the probability that they exceed CREDIT - 17,714 below exp(-20); outside that event every preflight passes, because the credit left is at least 17,714 >= CM(T). The time bound charges the whole credit whether or not the premise holds; success 0.39 holds under H1', H4', H_G_cluster and this premise (proof.md 10.3, 10.4).
heuristics.scope: U for every one of the RUN_STEPS outer steps of proof.md 9.1, that is, for every member of every one of the RUN_CONTEXTS contexts (9.8), as a function of the context's outer words and the member, with S = 0x5f, the masks X of the filter of Section 8, nu by formula (V) of 9.7, the solver of 9.4 with (G7) and (G15) and the unit costs of Section 11; the mean is over all outer steps, passing or not, with the zeros counted.
heuristics.extrapolation: u_M is GPT-6 Astra's bound in model M (proof.md 10.3: Q = Y9, omega, C2.c1, C2.b1, Y1 + w12 and Y12 independent uniform words, a uniform member, everything else computed): a call has probability 279,070,422,111 / 2^50, the per-call part A(T) has the exact mean 1383624064/266237 (recounted by the participant in integers from the certificate of Section 8) and the blocks add at most 22422672/266237 per call (Astra's proof, cited), so u_M = p_call (1383624064/266237 + 22422672/266237) exactly. Measured, untrusted by the harness (proof.md Section 13, not preregistered): on 2^32 real outer steps with the lines of the searched instance and 2^32 with flags 11, fresh Philox4x32-10 words per step, a participant reimplementation of the solver ran every call (1,063,703 and 1,065,105 calls, no call above its C15(T)) and its ledger U averaged 1.298456 and 1.300374 per outer step, each with a standard error of about 0.0013, against u_M = 1.3090 and 1.01 u_M = 1.322107; 99.1 per cent of U is the part A(T), a function of T. The declared program's own 1,031 calls over 4,096 trials averaged 5,195.5 units of U per call.
heuristics.limitations: Not proved: the words of the sampler are not proved to have the law of model M, so u_M is not a property of the sampler, and the tree part of u_M is a cited proof. The measurement is one pseudorandom generator, made after the design, with a reimplementation of the solver, and it counts each executed block at its upper unit cost, not executed instructions. If the premise fails, the credit can halt the run with failure, which lowers the success probability and not the time bound. This premise replaces the cap-moment premise of the credit of our earlier entries.

heuristics.statement: Supporting; stated for the advice record of proof.md Section 12. This is the premise H_G_cluster of GPT Sol's answer CM 5. For a context C of the run let G(C) be the number of its 84,261 batches (2,341 representative batches and five partner batches per cluster, in the order of proof.md 9.9) that hold a member whose test-(2) mask meets S, counted without halts; G(C) is a function of the seven outer words alone, and before any halt it is exactly the number of fills of the context (proof.md 9.8, 9.9). Premise: for a context with uniform outer words, E[G(C)] <= 12,466. Use, proved given the premise (GPT Sol, answer CM 5): the fill budget is G_BUDGET = ceil(12,466 RUN_CONTEXTS) + 84,261 s = 15,220,080,066,873,262,535 with s = ceil(sqrt(10 RUN_CONTEXTS)); the G(C) of the contexts are independent and lie between 0 and 84,261, so Hoeffding's inequality over the contexts bounds the overflow by exp(-2 s^2 / RUN_CONTEXTS) <= exp(-20); a halt only stops fills. No law of the batches, lanes or members inside a context is used. Reaching the budget halts with failure; the time bound charges G_BUDGET + 1 fills.
heuristics.scope: G(C) for every one of the RUN_CONTEXTS contexts of proof.md 9.1, with the cluster map of 9.9 (clusters of 32 members that differ in bits 10 to 14 of e1), the batches of seven in the order of 9.9 and the direct table T2 restricted to S; the mean is over contexts with uniform outer words.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured, untrusted by the harness (proof.md Section 13): a sample of 2^24 = 16,777,216 contexts with SHAKE256 outer words, G counted exactly by a graphics-card program that agreed on 4,096 contexts with a Python mirror built from the declared program's own functions: sum 208,495,306,067, mean 12,427.289 (standard error 1.276), largest 31,214. One-sided Hoeffding at confidence 1 - exp(-7) with range 84,261 bounds the mean by 12,465.77...; in exact integers 2 (n g - sum)^2 >= 7 * 84,261^2 * n holds at g = 12,466 and fails at 12,465, so 12,466 is the least integer this bound supports. The empirical Bernstein and bounded KL bounds of the same sample are 12,432.25 and 12,453.82.
heuristics.limitations: Not proved: the mean of G for uniform outer words. The sample comes from one pseudorandom generator; its protocol was preregistered for a lower bound, which the sample rejects, and 12,466 is the confidence bound of the same sample, not a preregistered value. If the premise fails, the fill budget can halt the run with failure, which lowers the success probability and not the time bound.
